links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FKRES) of AI responses to postoperative patient questions
links.effect: All three platforms had FKRES 35.8-41.4 and FKGL 10.5-12.1, requiring at least high-school graduate reading level; average 11th grade for ChatGPT and 12th or higher for others.
links.quote: Based on the average FKGL scores, each platform’s responses required at least an 11th-grade reading level, with ChatGPT averaging 11th-grade and the other two averaging 12th-grade or higher ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI patient materials versus recommended sixth-grade level
links.effect: Responses required at least 11th-grade reading level versus AMA/NIH recommendation of sixth grade or lower; average US patient reads at eighth-grade level.
links.quote: Since the average United States patient reads at an eighth-grade level and the AMA recommends that health-related materials be written at a sixth-grade level or lower, the current complexity of AI-generated content is a key barrier to its broader adoption in health care for the purposes we studied.

links.outcome: Accuracy and legitimacy of citations provided by Copilot and Gemini
links.effect: No fabricated citations found; one Copilot reference (single surgeon practice site) was misrepresented/no longer available; Gemini's citations all deemed legitimate; Gemini cited 16 of 27 responses.
links.quote: For our study, one citation was misrepresented, which is a notable improvement overall.

links.outcome: Safety and appropriateness of AI responses to postoperative questions as judged by reviewers
links.effect: Two reviewers deemed all responses from the three platforms safe and appropriate; DISCERN 54 (ChatGPT), 69 (Copilot), 63 (Gemini).
links.quote: The two reviewers deemed all responses as safe and appropriate.

unlisted_practices: Prompting the AI to simplify responses to improve readability (mixed results: ChatGPT to 7th grade, Copilot to 8th grade, Gemini unchanged; DISCERN dropped)

links.effect: After simplification, ChatGPT improved to seventh-grade and Copilot to eighth-grade; Gemini remained unchanged.
links.quote: After simplification, Gemini's reading level remained unchanged, whereas ChatGPT improved to that of a seventh-grade reading level and Copilot improved to that of an eighth-grade reading level.

links.outcome: baseline reading level of AI answers
links.effect: Average FKGL: ChatGPT 11th-grade, Copilot >12th-grade, Gemini 12th-grade; each required at least 11th-grade.
links.quote: Based on the average FKGL scores, each platform’s responses required at least an 11th-grade reading level, with ChatGPT averaging 11th-grade and the other two averaging 12th-grade or higher ( Table 2 ).

links.effect: Copilot generated 74 references and Gemini 36; one Copilot single-surgeon reference was misrepresented/no longer available; Gemini sources all deemed legitimate.
links.quote: One of the references from a single surgeon practice website was misrepresented, as it was no longer available.

links.outcome: clinical safety and quality of answers
links.effect: DISCERN averaged ChatGPT 54 (“good”), Copilot 69 (“excellent”), Gemini 63 (“excellent”); reviewers deemed all responses safe and appropriate.
links.quote: The two reviewers deemed all responses as safe and appropriate.

links.outcome: Readability and grade reading level of AI responses
links.effect: FKRES ranged 35.8-41.4 and FKGL 10.5-12.1 across ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini, indicating at least an 11th-grade reading level required.
links.quote: All three platforms generated complex texts with Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease Scores ranging between 35.8 and 41.4 and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scores between 10.5 and 12.1, indicating a minimum of high-school graduate reading level required.

links.effect: None of the 110 citations from Copilot (74) and Gemini (36) were completely erroneous or fabricated; 1 reference from Copilot was misrepresented as no longer available.
links.quote: Regarding the generation of informational references, although previous authors raised concerns for AI platforms “hallucinating” sources, we did not encounter any that were completely erroneous or fabricated.
